title: Dhamaal 4 Just Sent the Gang to Sea — With Pirates, Ghosts and a Mountain of Gold. The Trailer Lands July 10.
excerpt: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh and Jaaved Jaaferi are back chasing treasure, and this time the franchise has gone full adventure-comedy.
body:
There's a moment in the **Dhamaal 4** trailer where one character is warned, deadpan: "Listen, brother. This is a family film. None of that is allowed here." It's a wink to the audience, an apology in advance, and a mission statement all at once. Two decades in, the *Dhamaal* franchise knows exactly what it is — and the fourth chapter has no interest in pretending otherwise.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

The makers unveiled the trailer on June 12, and the madness machine is running again. This time, though, the gang has traded small-time chaos for something far bigger: a gold-chasing adventure across the open sea, complete with pirates, animals, accidents, mistaken identities and — in a first for the series — seemingly supernatural ghosts. **Ajay Devgn** leads the ensemble, with **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh**, **Jaaved Jaaferi**, **Ravi Kishan** and **Sanjay Mishra** all back for the ride, joined by Esha Gupta, Sanjeeda Shaikh, Anjali Anand and Upendra Limaye in key roles.


![Ajay Devgn — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Ajay_Devgn_at_the_trailer_launch_of_Raid_2.jpg)



> **"None of that is allowed here." It's a wink to the audience, an apology in advance, and a mission statement all at once."**



The setup is franchise-perfect in its simplicity: a mountain of treasure is within reach, and every member of the group wants it for themselves. What follows is a relay race of greed, rivalry and dumb luck, where each step toward the gold triggers another disaster. The trailer leans hard into the series' old-school comic rhythm — physical gags, slapstick pratfalls, jungle madness and a rapid-fire chain of misunderstandings, all stitched together at a pace that barely lets you breathe.

> "Watch the biggest family entertainer Dhamaal 4 in cinemas worldwide from 10th July!"

That's the official promise, and director **Indra Kumar** has clearly built this one for the big screen. The makers turned the trailer launch into a full event experience at Imagicaa, transforming the venue to mirror the film's adventurous, larger-than-life world — a 60-foot poster, a manufactured waterfall, the works. It's the kind of theatrical showmanship that signals confidence, and early reactions suggest it's earned. One viewer called it the best trailer among recent comedy films; others singled out the scenic, big-canvas comedy as a genuine step up for the series.


![Arshad Warsi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9e/Arshad-Warsi.jpg)


What's interesting is how far the franchise has drifted from its origins. *Dhamaal* began in 2007 with Riteish, Arshad, Jaaved, Ashish Chaudhary and Sanjay Dutt scrambling after hidden money. *Total Dhamaal* brought Ajay Devgn into the fold and turned it into a jungle escapade. Now **Dhamaal 4**, a direct sequel to *Total Dhamaal*, pushes the canvas out to sea and into the supernatural — pirates and ghosts are new territory for a series that started with five idiots and a treasure map. It's a calculated bet that the audience wants the same comic DNA wrapped in a bigger, more cinematic package.


Produced by Ajay Devgn alongside Bhushan Kumar and Krishan Kumar under the **T-Series** and Devgn Films banners, the film is positioned squarely as a theatre-first, family-friendly entertainer. And the July release date is no accident — it slots Dhamaal 4 into the heart of the summer comedy window, just weeks after Akshay Kumar's *Welcome To The Jungle* arrives in late June. The message is unmistakable: 2026's monsoon belongs to ensemble comedy, and Bollywood is betting big that audiences are hungry to laugh in a packed hall again.

For the diaspora, this is comfort food of the highest order. *Dhamaal* films travel well — they're loud, visual, light on subtext and heavy on the kind of physical comedy that needs no cultural footnotes. A worldwide theatrical release on **July 10** means families across the US, UK and Canada can make it a weekend outing, and given T-Series' track record, a streaming home will almost certainly follow. The cast's pedigree helps too: Arshad Warsi alone has three films — *Welcome To The Jungle*, *Dhamaal 4* and the Rajkumar Hirani series *Pritam And Pedro* — landing within a fortnight, a comedy-season hat-trick that says a lot about where the box office winds are blowing.

Will it be high art? Of course not. Will it be the funniest, busiest, most chaotic two hours you can spend in a theatre this July? On the evidence of this trailer — the gang squabbling over gold while ghosts and pirates close in — that's exactly the pitch. The treasure hunt is on, and the only question left is who's foolish enough to think they'll be the one to walk away with the loot.
